rules: /// Whether `path`, an already-resolved command answer, is an ocx-generated launcher
/// trampoline. POSIX: [`TRAMPOLINE_MARKER`] is the whole second line of the first
/// [`TRAMPOLINE_PROBE_BYTES`] of a regular file. Windows: a `.exec` sidecar sits beside the
/// resolved `<stem>.exe`, or the resolved path's own extension is `.exec`.
/// It runs after the `PATH` exclusion of [`Env::resolve_command_excluding`], never in its
/// place, so each guard keeps its own reachable red state and a test can tell which one
/// caught an input. Matching the file rather than a directory list is what catches a
/// trampoline from a second project home on the same `PATH`.
/// A non-regular file answers false without being opened, and any I/O error answers false.
/// Failing closed, as `resolves_inside` in `ocx launcher shim` does, would turn a transient
/// `EACCES` on an unrelated binary into a refusal to run an ordinary command, since this runs
/// on every resolution including `/bin/sh`; the `PATH` exclusion still backstops it, and an
/// unreadable file is no worse than an absent one.
// Line 2 is matched whole, never by `contains()` or anywhere in the prefix: a looser match
// refuses an ordinary tool that embeds the string, and a package launcher whose baked
// `$OCX_HOME` spells the marker, breaking `ocx launcher exec`; nothing interpolated reaches
// lines 1 or 2. The prefix bound keeps the probe to one `read(2)` before every `exec`;
// `a_marker_beyond_the_probe_window_is_not_refused` fails if the bound is widened.
// `ocx_util::fs::read_bounded` does not fit: it errors past the cap, a trampoline body passes
// 256 bytes once the project root is about 146 characters deep, and the fail-open arm turns
// that error into "not a trampoline" for deep checkouts while shallow-root tests stay green.
// `is_file()` is checked before the open, or a FIFO on `PATH` blocks the `exec` forever.
// Windows has no content check: trampoline and lazy-shim-slot `.exe`s hardlink one blob, so
// a content match refuses shim slots. The own-`.exec` refusal is required because `which`
// treats any extension as executable, so a `PATHEXT` with `.EXEC` resolves the sidecar itself.
OCX-02.tags: contract: what it answers, POSIX/Windows signals, non-regular and I/O-error answer false; guards: runs after (not instead of) the PATH exclusion, fail-open vs sibling resolves_inside, whole-line-2 anchor (not contains), prefix bound (test a_marker_beyond_the_probe_window_is_not_refused replaces the widening guard), not read_bounded, is_file before open (FIFO), no Windows content match, own-.exec refusal; why: file-not-directory matching, nothing interpolated reaches lines 1-2, unreadable==absent; implementation hazards moved to a plain // comment at the same position; dropped: process IDs C-069/C-010/C-028/D-V1/D-V12/D-V15/E-21/WP-6, stale 'why this has a body' stub provenance, validation-row argument (Item 37/WP-12e), design-story prose

rules: /// The deduped union of config-declared and env-declared plain-HTTP hosts, less any name a
/// SYSTEM-scope (`/etc/ocx/config.toml`) `[registries."<name>"]` entry states `insecure = false`
/// for, `OCX_INSECURE_REGISTRIES` included. `None` subtracts nothing, and a non-system
/// `insecure = false` revokes nothing. The subtraction is required, or one env var defeats the
/// lock [`RegistryConfig::merge`](crate::RegistryConfig::merge) enforces against lower tiers.
/// Granting is byte-exact on `host[:port]`, case included, matching the transport's
/// `ClientProtocol::HttpsExcept` membership test: `registry.corp` does not cover
/// `registry.corp:5001`, and a mis-cased entry grants nothing, which fails closed
/// (`host_and_port_are_one_opaque_name`). Each gate compares its own resolved host string;
/// they agree for `host[:port]`, but Docker Hub resolves differently for the transport and for
/// [`canonicalize_registry`](ocx_oci::auth::registry_url::canonicalize_registry), so no spelling
/// of it can be granted plaintext, deliberately (see [`ocx_oci::auth::login`]).
/// Revoking is normalised in `same_registry_name`, because an exact match there fails open
/// (CWE-319/CWE-522). Without ASCII case folding, `OCX_INSECURE_REGISTRIES=Registry.Corp:5000`
/// or a lower-tier `[registries."Registry.Corp:5000"]` walks past a lock on `registry.corp:5000`.
/// Without numeric port normalisation, `registry.corp:05000` reaches the locked TCP 5000 in
/// plaintext.
/// Known residual: a lock on `registry.corp` does not reach `registry.corp:80`, nor the
/// reverse. No default port is filled in, because the four consumers span both schemes and
/// any constant is wrong for some of them.

rules: /// Drops every occurrence of `value` from a `PATH`-style value, using [`move_to_front`]'s

/// as `Shell::remove_list_element` does, because the live environment spells a

/// resolves a claimed-but-unshipped name back to the shim, and `execvp` re-enters it forever.
/// **Precondition** (as [`move_to_front`]): `value` is one directory with no `PATH_SEPARATOR`.
/// Comparison is segment-exact to match the emitted shell snippets, so a trailing slash,
/// a symlink alias or a differently spelled root survives. This is not a containment check;
/// callers that must fail closed re-check the resolved answer against the resolved directory.

// which `try_acquire` must retry or fail spuriously. Best-effort: a leftover sidecar is harmless.

rules: /** Basename of the ad-blocker-safe alias copy of a package root, written beside the package's
* own CAS directory: `p/<ns>/<pkg>/_root.json`. The site fetches the alias because a root URL

* matches one of their ~800 unanchored `/<word>.js` rules (`/hawkeye.js` blocks

* still written; the alias is an extra copy for the site's fetch, never a wire-format change. */

rules: """Look `name` up on `search_path`, entry by entry, refusing unsafe hits.
A hit in `cwd` (with `windows`) or in a group- or other-writable directory
(without it) is refused as a binary-injection vector (CWE-426).
Returns:
The first acceptable hit, as an absolute path, or `None`.
# Each entry's hit is vetted rather than trusting one `shutil.which` call, which on Windows
# searches the current directory ahead of PATH and so trusts a binary planted there.
# `cwd` and each hit are resolved first, or a relative entry like `.` slips past the `cwd` comparison.
# The hit is resolved, or the caller is handed a relative path that goes stale on the next `chdir`.
PY-05.tags: contract: summary, refusal rules per windows/cwd (folded windows+cwd args), Returns absolute-or-None; pointer: CWE-426; guards moved to plain # comments: per-entry vetting vs single shutil.which (cwd-first on Windows), resolve before cwd comparison (relative '.'), resolve hit (stale after chdir); dropped: tautological Args name/search_path and section scaffolding.

rules: """Return the digest the manifest body must have, or `None` when none is required.
A remote read off `CANONICAL_DIST_HOST` or with a mirror in play needs a pin,
since TLS there proves reachability rather than authenticity. A local source
(`url` and `origin` are `None`) is exempt: its bytes have provenance, and
hashing them against a digest derived from themselves proves nothing.
A `dist/<sha256>.json` URL pins itself. That digest must come from the
caller-supplied URL string before any request goes out, or a redirect could
choose which digest the body is checked against.
Raises:
DistManifestError: A pin is required and missing, or the URL and the
explicit `sha256=` name different digests.
PY-06.tags: contract: summary (Returns folded in), when a pin is required, local-source None url/origin, snapshot URL self-pin, Raises; why: TLS proves reachability not authenticity, local bytes self-hash proves nothing (one sentence each); guard: digest from caller-supplied URL before any request, or a redirect chooses it; pointer: CANONICAL_DIST_HOST (resolves); dropped: tautological Args source/mirrored and section scaffolding.

rules: """Build an ocx argv: `[exe, *global_flags, *command, *positionals, --, *child]`.
`global_flags` precede the subcommand because ocx's clap grammar accepts
global flags nowhere else. `command` is the SDK-composed subcommand path
plus its flags; `positionals` are identifiers ocx resolves itself. `child`
is the argv of a process ocx hosts (`run`, `package exec`), placed behind
`--` where a leading dash is safe; when it is empty no `--` is written.
Raises:
ValueError: A positional starts with `-`, so ocx would parse it as a
flag (CWE-88).
PY-07.tags: guard: global flags before subcommand (clap accepts them nowhere else), leading-dash positional raises (kept in Raises, CWE-88 pointer); contract: summary layout, command/positionals/child roles, child behind --, empty child writes no --; dropped: Returns 'The argv, ready for run_command or spawn' (tautology), tautological exe/global_flags Args, duplicate 'Always guarded' clause (covered by Raises).
